item.title: Upside-down cantilever cracks open timber hotel by BIG
item.description:
【AI 精简版】 AI-condensed version. This text was produced by an LLM from the original article and may omit details. The original link at the end is the only authoritative source.

Why it is here: In-depth architectural analysis with clear, well-structured English and original reporting.

BIG has designed a timber hotel with a zigzagging, stepped design in Thun, Switzerland. The 13,000-square-metre Nachwachsende Stadt development includes four timber buildings with a cantilevered corner volume housing hotels. BIG aims to reduce carbon footprint and achieve SNBS Gold standard with green roofs and photovoltaic panels. Construction is set to begin in 2028.

Mexico City's Antara expansion features four monumental slides by artist Carsten Höller, integrating play into a mixed-use development. The slides, up to 125 feet tall, connect retail, offices, and a hotel. The project, part of Antara's 20-year evolution, includes a public garden, new art venue, and retail expansion. Höller's slides open December 2026, offering a unique way to navigate the complex.
